title: PREM Rugby opens 12-team expansion process
article_text:
The initial Request for Information stage is open to clubs, investors and authorised representatives. No formal bid or investment commitment is required at this stage, with a tender process due to follow later in 2027. The introduction of two additional teams remains subject to readiness.

Successful entrants would need to acquire a P share, currently valued at approximately £20m. Spending at least one season in the second-tier Champ is also reported to be a condition of entry.

Former top-flight clubs Worcester Warriors and London Irish are among those reported as potential applicants. Coventry, Ealing Trailfinders and Cornish Pirates are also expected to consider the process, although no club has yet been confirmed for either of the additional places.

Prem Rugby has indicated that new franchises could also be considered, particularly where they would expand the league’s geographical footprint. Yorkshire is reported to be one area of interest, while developments involving Wasps are also being monitored.

The process comes amid increasing investment in English club rugby. Recent ownership and investment activity has involved the owners of AFC Bournemouth at Exeter Chiefs, Red Bull at Newcastle Red Bulls and James Dyson at Bath Rugby. Prem Rugby chief executive Simon Massie-Taylor is also meeting potential investors in the United States as the league develops its expansion plans.

The Welsh Rugby Union has separately expressed interest in Welsh clubs joining an expanded competition, although reports indicate that Prem Rugby’s current focus remains on adding English teams.

The expansion would increase the top flight to 12 clubs from 2029/30, subject to the outcome of the information and tender stages and prospective entrants meeting the league’s financial and operational requirements.

title: Skydance’s Kanal 5 and HBO Max net Ski Classic rights in Sweden
article_text:
Ski Classics, the Europe-based long-distance cross-country skiing series, has secured its visibility in Sweden after signing a new rights agreement with commercial broadcaster Kanal 5 and streaming service HBO Max.

The partnership gives Kanal 5 and HBO Max, both owned by global media conglomerate Skydance, exclusive rights in the country to the first 12 events scheduled for the Ski Classics World Championship 2026-27 season.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The season begins on December 11 and runs through April 4, with 15 events held across six countries: Austria, Switzerland, the Czech Republic, Sweden, Italy, and Norway.

The final three events of the season, the women’s and men’s Oxberg-Mora Sprint and Vasaloppet, will be aired in Sweden by public service broadcaster SVT.

Roberto Vacchi, commentator for road cycling’s elite Tour de France, will lead the pair's coverage, bringing experience from the Ski Classics.

The season will open with the Bad Gastein Prologue in Austria and end with the Grand Finale Summit 2 Senja in Norway.

The new deal comes shortly after organizers of the Ski Classics unveiled a rights extension in Finland with TV5 and HBO Max earlier this month.

The contract renewal sees the two platforms – both part of the Skydance media empire – continuing as the exclusive home in Finland for Ski Classics for the upcoming 2026-27 season.

As has been the case in previous campaigns, every event will be shown live on the HBO Max streaming platform, while most will also be available free-to-air (FTA) via linear broadcaster TV5.

title: Blast and Fever partner in live events ticketing deal
article_text:
Ticketing and entertainment tech provider Fever has entered into a deal with heavyweight esports organization Blast, running through 2029.

Through a tie-up unveiled today, Fever becomes the esports organization's exclusive ticketing partner across its entire live events portfolio.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Fever will work to integrate ticket searches, purchasing, transfers, and event access into one platform.

Fever's technology will be integrated into the various Blast online platforms, while tickets will also be sold through Fever's sales channels.

In addition, Fever will provide Blast with on-site ticketing operations, including "secure access-control technology and box-office terminals, alongside 24/7 multilingual customer support."

Marketing and promotion will also be provided by Fever through the deal.

Overall, this forms part of the wider Blast efforts to ramp up the live events side of its business.

James Woollard, Blast's vice president of destinations and marketing, commented: "Partnering with Fever allows us to bring more of that journey together in one place, making it easier for fans to discover our events, buy with confidence, securely resell or transfer tickets and personalise their experience after purchase.”

This month has already seen Fever unveil a deal with the Premier Jumping League (PJL), the new global show jumping competition launching next year.

In mid-October, meanwhile, Fever was announced as the ticketing platform partner for the X Games action sports property.

title: "Disappointed" and "no excuses" – Oliver Bearman frustrated by lack of 2027 F1 contract
article_text:
Following confirmation that Liam Lawson and Valtteri Bottas will remain on the grid, only one seat formally remains vacant for the 2027 Formula 1 season. It is the Haas seat currently occupied by Oliver Bearman.

There is virtually no doubt in the paddock that Bearman will also be on the F1 grid next year, but he finds the delay extremely frustrating, as he made clear in Las Vegas when speaking to media including Motorsport.com.

"There is nothing new to say. If I'm honest, I'm quite disappointed that I'm sitting here at round 20 without a contract signed for next year. It's been a strange situation, but we're getting there," Bearman said.

"All I can say is that it's a bit disappointing and obviously it's not ideal for a driver's confidence and things like that. Of course, I know that I've done a good job this year, but the fact that I don't know what I'm doing next year is not ideal. I'll tell you that much."

Bearman preferred to avoid the question of who exactly he is disappointed with during the media day in Sin City: "I'm not going to comment on that."

It is particularly frustrating for Bearman that he feels good progress has been made in recent weeks, yet it has still not been enough to announce an agreement, while all his fellow drivers on the grid already know where they stand.

"It's very clear that I'm trying to stay at Haas and that I deserve to stay at Haas. At least I feel that way. It's just a strange situation," he said.

"I really thought that we had made decent progress in the last triple header, but maybe it doesn't seem that way. It's a little disappointing. I hope that we can get to the end of this weekend and that I have some good news to tell you."

Bearman completely ruled out racing for any F1 team other than Haas in 2027, something that already appears impossible given that all the other seats have been filled.

Asked by Motorsport.com whether there is a risk that he will ultimately have to settle for a compromise – signing a deal for 2027 but not getting the long-term prospects he wants for the years beyond – he continued: "My goal for 2027 is very clear. I think we have unfinished business here.

"Then looking further into the future, it's not really in my hands, let's say it like that. It's not my avenue. I'm driving the car, but from what I've understood, it's been a challenging one."

The delay appears to be mainly related to his longer-term prospects. In Mexico, Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu dismissed speculation about excessive salary demands as “complete nonsense”, suggesting that the discussions are more likely to revolve around Bearman's future beyond 2027.

The 21-year-old Briton is still affiliated with Ferrari, but acknowledges that it is difficult to get any guarantees about a potential future with the Scuderia.

"I'm under contract with Ferrari. Ferrari have given me this incredible opportunity to step into F1 with them for the first time," he said. "I'm still a Ferrari junior driver and my ultimate dream is to race for Ferrari. They're the most iconic team and they're the first team that believed in me as a kid.

"It's still my ultimate dream, but there's no doubt that looking into the future, there may be some challenges there. There's no denying that, it's very clear. I don't really have much say in the matter. We just need to see how things develop over time."

Regardless of the exact cause and who is to blame, Bearman is particularly uncomfortable with still facing uncertainty with only a few weeks remaining until the winter break.

"Like I said, we are getting there, but it's not a good feeling to be sitting here with two races to go without things sorted out," he said.

"Even though I know that we're pretty much there, the fact is that we're not. There's no excuse for being here without a contract signed, quite honestly."

title: Hamilton insists there are no "trust" problems at Ferrari
article_text:
Lewis Hamilton has insisted there are zero “trust” problems at Ferrari despite him overruling strategic calls becoming a repeated occurrence across recent Formula 1 grands prix.

The seven-time world champion has ignored calls to pit in two of the last four rounds - Singapore and Brazil - with both backfiring on the Scuderia driver.

In Singapore he elected to keep track position under a virtual safety car, but on worn tyres he dropped from podium contention to sixth late on - for which he apologised afterwards.

Then in Brazil last time out, Hamilton stayed on slicks despite the rain intensifying and this led to a late spin at the final corner before pitting the following lap to eventually finish ninth.

Those instances came amid talk of fractious relations down at Ferrari but ahead of this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix, Hamilton confirmed all is well - particularly with his new-for-2026 race engineer Carlo Santi.

“It’s definitely not a trust thing, we’re constantly working on our communication,” said the 41-year-old.

"It's been a lot better this year. Carlo has done an amazing job and those particular two times, particularly the last time, was just I didn't have the information I needed.

“I got the call right at the last minute. We'll just continue to work on the processes. We're super united in what's working, in the right direction."

This year has been much improved for Hamilton, who is fourth in the standings with three rounds remaining, currently on 261 points compared to his total of 156 in 2025.

His first year in Ferrari colours was certainly underwhelming, but there have still been signs of improvement in 2026 despite it being a significant jump from last season.

Not only is that in reference to the strategic calls, but also his connection with team-mate Charles Leclerc, clashing on a few occasions and most notably in Mexico three weeks ago.

It cost Ferrari the win and Hamilton subsequently criticised Leclerc’s “do or die” attitude, before suggesting in Sao Paulo that the Monegasque races him harder than he does with other drivers.

That led to an hour-long meeting between both Scuderia drivers plus team boss Fred Vasseur and Hamilton and Leclerc are now confident that the issue has been resolved.

“Charles is a great driver,” said Hamilton. “The detail we went into about stuff like that, in terms of when we close the visor, it's very clear, we understand each other, we understand each other's boundaries and the ultimate goal, which is to get the best result for the team.

“So I don't feel like that will be a problem moving forward. I have no concerns or worries about racing him, and I don't think he does for me either.”

The talk surrounding the Mexico clash was naturally high, but Leclerc reckons that is a consequence of driving for Ferrari and all focus is now on securing runner-up in the constructors’ standings.

“Everything has been taken out of proportion,” said Leclerc. “I'm kind of used to it now, driving for Ferrari for so many years. But things are very often taken out of proportion.

“The goal is not always to agree and that will never happen. We can have different opinions and that was the case, for example, in Mexico.

“But just the fact of speaking eased all tensions and we were completely fine with it. It's not that we had to speak for an hour, even though it ended up lasting an hour, just because we had a good time.

“We started speaking about many other things in trying to bring the team and to help the team go forward.

“But the discussion about the tension was like maybe five or 10 minutes and then the air was clean and that's it.”

Ferrari heads into the Vegas race 95 points ahead of third-placed Red Bull and 142 behind Mercedes, who clinched its ninth title at Interlagos.

Celsius Is Turning Sports Sponsorships Into a Year-Round Brand Platform
article_text:
Celsius is building a sports marketing system rather than betting on one big sponsorship. The energy drink brand is combining college football, Formula 1, running communities and fitness competitions to make its better-for-you positioning visible wherever active consumers already gather.

Celsius became the official energy drink sponsor of ESPN’s College GameDay in August, with campus run clubs, tailgates and a multi-year partnership. The brand also used college football NIL deals with analyst Kirk Herbstreit, Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood and Oregon quarterback Dante Moore.

The important move is not the size of any individual deal. It is the way Celsius is connecting different sports environments to the same consumer promise.

At the New York City Marathon, the brand returned with a Club Celsius pop-up and a multi-day Brooklyn takeover. It also sponsored Diplo’s Run Club stops in New York, Chicago and Los Angeles. Earlier in the year, Celsius became the official global energy drink partner of the ATHX Games, a fitness competition.

That gives Live. Fit. Go., the 360-degree campaign launched in 2025 across television, paid and organic social, out-of-home and experiential marketing, more places to show up. A runner, college football fan and Formula 1 viewer may not share a sport, but they can still recognize the same brand behavior: Celsius is present around performance, movement and the rituals that surround them.

Celsius is also extending the strategy into premium global sports. The company signed British driver Jessica Hawkins ahead of the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix and continues its multi-year partnership with Aston Martin Aramco in Formula 1.

That range is deliberate. Celsius CMO Kyle Watson told Modern Retail that the brand is not defined by a single sport and wants to build connections across the sports landscape. The approach gives Celsius more chances to meet consumers in context, rather than asking one event or athlete to carry the entire brand story.

There is a practical lesson here for marketers. Sports sponsorship works harder when it creates repeatable participation around the rights deal: a run club, a campus activation, a fan event or a product ritual. The logo may create awareness, but the surrounding behavior gives the partnership a reason to be remembered.

Celsius is effectively using sports as a year-round distribution network for its positioning. The strategic consequence is that future growth will depend less on adding famous names and more on making each new partnership feel like another credible expression of the same active lifestyle.

title: Gctc Announces New Naming Rights Partnership
Big Sky Dips Toe Into Women’s Swimming Sponsorship with Five Members
article_text:
The Big Sky Conference will sponsor women’s swimming and diving in 2027-28, starting with a five-team field.

Member institutions Idaho, Northern Arizona, Northern Colorado and Utah Tech will join the league’s launch. University of Texas Rio Grande Valley will join for the first time as an affiliate member.

All five schools jump from the Mountain Pacific Sports Federation, whose expansion in women’s swimming to 24 teams appears to be a one-year gambit.

“We are absolutely thrilled to introduce women’s swimming and diving as the newest Big Sky-sponsored sport,” Big Sky Conference Commissioner Tom Wistrcill said in a press release last week. “In this era of college athletics, it’s particularly meaningful that our membership has leaned into crowning another team each year as a Big Sky champion and, in doing so, will create a direct pathway for additional Big Sky student-athletes to qualify for and participate in their respective NCAA championship. I applaud the administrations at our four current full members that sponsor this sport for embracing this opportunity, and on behalf of our entire membership also eagerly welcome the UTRGV Vaqueros to our conference as an affiliate.”

The Big Sky sponsored men’s swimming and diving from 1963-74. This is the first time that it will sponsor women’s swimming and diving. It is the 10th women’s sport and 17th total sport in the Big Sky’s championship portfolio.

“I’m very excited to see women’s swimming and diving join the Big Sky Conference,” Big Sky SAAC Executive Board member and Idaho diver Amelia Ward said. “As a student-athlete at the University of Idaho, I look forward to competing against universities that already share a competitive relationship with other athletic teams at our school. I believe this will foster camaraderie among student-athletes and strengthen our university’s athletic community.”

title: Mansoor bin Mohammed leads UAE delegation at 38th meeting of GCC Olympic Committee Presidents
article_text:
His Highness Sheikh Mansoor bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, President of the UAE Olympic Committee, led the UAE delegation at the 38th meeting of the Presidents of the Olympic Committees of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries, held in the Kingdom of Bahrain today.

Upon His Highness’s arrival at Bahrain International Airport, he was received by Sheikh Khalid bin Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, President of the Bahrain Olympic Committee. Ahead of the meeting, His Highness joined the Presidents of the Olympic Committees of GCC countries, for a group photograph.

The UAE delegation included His Excellency Faris Mohammed Al Mutawa, Secretary General of the UAE Olympic Committee; His Excellency Dr. Nasser Al Tamimi, Board Member of the Committee and Vice President of the UAE Judo Federation; and His Excellency Fahad Mohammed Salem bin Kardous Al Ameri, UAE Ambassador to the Kingdom of Bahrain.

The meeting discussed a range of topics aimed at strengthening Gulf sports cooperation, foremost among them supporting Doha’s bid to host the 2036 Olympic and Paralympic Games, developing the regulatory frameworks governing Gulf sports federations, and enabling the Sports Advisory Committee to fulfil its role at GCC multi-sport Games.

The discussions covered the final versions of the statutes governing Gulf sports federations, the procedures for establishing federations and relocating their headquarters between member states, and the mechanisms by which the Executive Office examines applications to establish federations and submits them to the Council of Olympic Committee Presidents. It also covered the continuous monitoring and evaluation of federation performance.

The meeting also examined the responsibilities of the Sports Advisory Committee at GCC multi-sport Games, alongside a proposal to establish a four-member subcommittee comprising representatives of the country holding the current presidency, the host country, the country due to assume the next presidency, and the General Secretariat. The proposed subcommittee would monitor preparations and the fulfilment of commitments by national Olympic committees, participate in coordination and technical meetings and meetings of chefs de mission, and follow competitions during the Games.

The discussions addressed the UAE’s initiative to host the fourth GCC Beach Games in 2027, following Bahrain’s withdrawal from hosting the event due to its commitment to hosting the Arab Games in the same year and the associated organisational, technical and logistical obligations. Discussions also covered follow-up on the completion of the necessary procedures and official approvals with the relevant authorities in the UAE.

In the same context, the meeting reviewed a proposal by the UAE Olympic Committee to hold a Sports Law and Management Conference on the sidelines of the 2027 GCC Beach Games, should they be held in the UAE.

The meeting reviewed the final report on the fourth GCC Games – Doha 2026, covering its data and information, technical and organisational aspects, challenges and recommendations. It also discussed referring the report to the Executive Office and the relevant committees for review and necessary action, while expressing appreciation for Qatar’s efforts in making the Games a success.

The meeting further discussed the schedule of GCC multi-sport Games for 2029–2032 and aligning their dates with regional and international sporting commitments. Discussions took into account Saudi Arabia’s earlier withdrawal from hosting the 2024 Gulf Indoor and Martial Arts Games, the UAE’s initiative to host the 2027 GCC Beach Games, Kuwait’s hosting of the second GCC Youth Games in 2028, and Qatar’s withdrawal from hosting the Games scheduled for 2029–2031 due to its commitments to major sporting events. The meeting also explored the possibility of Bahrain, Saudi Arabia and the Sultanate of Oman hosting the remaining Games, depending on their respective circumstances and capabilities.

Other matters included following up on the implementation of decisions taken at the 37th meeting of the Council of GCC Olympic Committee Presidents and coordinating with Saudi Arabia, which will assume the presidency for the next term, to determine the date and venue of the Council’s 39th meeting, to be preceded by a preparatory meeting of the Executive Office.

title: Wellstar Health named as naming rights partner for Atlanta City FC women’s soccer facility
article_text:
The recently minted Atlanta City FC pro women's soccer team in metro Atlanta is ramping up operations and it now has a partner for its training facility.

Wellstar Health System was announced as the Atlanta City FC's naming rights partner for the team's training facility, making the facility the Wellstar Performance Center, according to officials.

The AMB Sports and Entertainment company said Wellstar was named on the facility as part of a joint commitment to supporting female athletes.

As part of the agreement, Wellstar will work with AMBSE for several years to construct a world-class facility specifically for female athletes.

"From the outset, we committed to constructing a state-of-the-art performance center for Atlanta City FC and equipping our club with the necessary resources to compete for championships," said President of Soccer, AMBSE Mauricio Culebro. "We are excited to have Wellstar help bring this vision to life and lend their expertise to ensure our athletes receive best-in-class care to help them perform at their best. We are also confident Wellstar Performance Center will serve as a key recruiting tool as we look to welcome world-class players to Atlanta City FC ahead of our NWSL debut in 2028."

In addition to building the facility together through the partnership with Atlanta City FC and AMBSE, Wellstar Health System will also serve as the team's official healthcare provider.

Wellstar will also be the training apparel partner for the club team, according to the announcement. This includes matchday activations and fan engagement at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, digital signage and match sponsorship.

The two companies will also create a joint philanthropic program to host women's health events and orthopedics at the Wellstar Performance Center, once construction is complete.

"Atlanta City FC and Wellstar share a commitment to helping people thrive, both on and off the field," said Ketul J. Patel, President and CEO of Wellstar Health System." Through this partnership, we'll support the club's athletes while creating new ways to connect with women, families, and communities across the region. We are honored to be selected as the club's healthcare partner and to work alongside an organization that reflects Arthur Blank's long-standing commitment to improving lives across Georgia."

Patel said the team-up is "a reflection of the exceptional care our physicians and team members provide every day," adding that the health system was looking forward to the fruits of the partnership.

AMBSE owner Arthur Blank said he was thrilled to welcome Wellstar Health System as the official healthcare provider for Atlanta City FC.

"Our family of businesses and Wellstar share a foundational belief about the importance of making a difference in the community, and we are proud to represent a Georgia-based organization at the home of our new club," Blank said in a statement. "I'd like to thank Ketul Patel and the entire team at Wellstar for their unwavering commitment to supporting our athletes, as well as our executive leadership team for bringing this partnership to life."

title: Ondas Partners with Aston Martin F1 Team in Multi-Year Technology Collaboration
article_text:
Ondas Inc. (Nasdaq: ONDS), a developer of autonomous systems and mission-critical technologies, has announced a multi-year partnership with the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team, becoming a Global Partner of the British racing organization.

The Ondas Aston Martin Formula One partnership will focus on engineering collaboration, technology exchange and data-driven decision-making under a shared initiative called “Speed to Decision.”

The agreement also provides Ondas with a global marketing platform to engage customers, investors and business partners, beginning with branding on Aston Martin’s Formula One car at the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The collaboration brings together two organizations operating in different industries but facing similar engineering challenges involving reliability, complex data and time-sensitive decisions.

Ondas develops autonomous systems, robotics and integrated sensing technologies for defense, homeland security, public safety and industrial applications.

Aston Martin Aramco competes in Formula One, where teams continuously analyze vehicle performance, environmental conditions and operational information to make decisions during races.

The partnership is intended to explore how engineering practices developed in these environments can inform technology development and operational execution.

“This partnership brings together two organizations grounded in engineering excellence, rapid innovation and high-performance execution,” said Eric Brock, Chairman and CEO of Ondas.

Brock said the agreement provides opportunities for technical collaboration while expanding Ondas’ engagement with customers, partners and investors.

Beginning in 2027, the partnership will include an annual Engineering Leadership workshop at Aston Martin’s AMR Technology Campus in Silverstone, England.

The workshops will bring together engineering and technology teams from both organizations to examine approaches to rapid development, iterative testing and decision-making.

The companies intend to identify practices that could produce measurable benefits within their respective operations.

However, the announcement does not identify specific joint products, research programs or technology transfers resulting from the agreement.

The partnership’s central theme, “Speed to Decision,” reflects the importance of converting complex information into timely operational decisions.

For Ondas, that concept relates to autonomous platforms and mission-critical technologies operating in demanding environments.

In Formula One, engineering teams must interpret vehicle telemetry, track conditions and strategic information while making decisions under significant time pressure.

Ryan Hartman, President and CEO of Ondas Sentinel, highlighted the similarities.

“Formula One demonstrates what happens when engineering, information and human judgment operate as one system,” Hartman said.

He described the partnership as an opportunity to exchange ideas about using advanced technology to support precise decisions at operational speed.

While the organizations see potential value in sharing engineering practices, the agreement does not announce the integration of Ondas drone technology into Aston Martin’s racing operations.

The partnership will make its public debut during the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Ondas branding will appear on the nose of Aston Martin’s Formula One car, with additional branding on driver race suits beginning in the 2027 season.

The agreement also includes digital content, hospitality experiences and opportunities for engagement with customers and business partners.

Jefferson Slack, Managing Director of Commercial and Marketing at Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team, welcomed Ondas as a Global Partner.

“Formula One provides a unique platform for bringing businesses together, building relationships and creating new opportunities,” Slack said.

He highlighted the team’s trackside hospitality and knowledge-sharing opportunities as elements of the relationship.

The financial terms of the partnership were not disclosed.

Ondas provides autonomous and unmanned systems for government, defense and commercial customers.

The company develops technologies intended to support operations where reliable information, automation and rapid decision-making are important.

The Aston Martin partnership is primarily an engineering collaboration and commercial engagement agreement rather than an announced drone development or defense procurement program.

For Ondas, the arrangement creates opportunities to exchange technical knowledge while increasing international visibility for its autonomous systems business.

The multi-year agreement establishes a framework for cooperation between Ondas and Aston Martin Aramco beginning with the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Annual engineering workshops are scheduled to begin in 2027, alongside continued marketing and stakeholder engagement activities.

The Ondas Aston Martin Formula One partnership illustrates how companies developing autonomous and mission-critical technologies are exploring relationships with high-performance engineering organizations outside the traditional aerospace and defense sectors.

The value of the technical collaboration will depend on the results of future workshops and any subsequent development initiatives.

For more information, visit Ondas and Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

title: Disney+ premieres The Pursuit: F1 Academy before Las Vegas
Lewis Hamilton identifies 'main focus' ahead of Las Vegas Grand Prix as Ferrari eye 'big changes' for 2027
article_text:
Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc are targeting a strong end to 2026 as Ferrari fight for P2 and look ahead to next season.

Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc have stressed the importance of finishing the 2026 season strongly as Ferrari look to bounce back from a challenging Sao Paulo Grand Prix, with the team focused on securing P2 in the Constructors' Championship and gathering valuable information ahead of next year.

Ferrari arrive in Las Vegas after Leclerc and Hamilton finished eighth and ninth respectively in Brazil, but Hamilton remains determined to deliver a result that would mean a great deal to those working behind the scenes at Maranello.

"The Constructors' Championship is the main focus," Hamilton said during media day in Las Vegas. "The main focus is making sure we solidify second in the Constructors' for the team, because that's something that means a huge amount to everyone back at the factory, but especially to me also.

"That's what we're working towards and then, if we're able to do well and keep in the battle for these last few races, maybe we can climb back up from fourth and hopefully be in the top three."

Looking ahead to 2027, Hamilton explained that the remaining three races would also offer opportunities to experiment with different setups and gather data, despite Ferrari having no new components available to test.

"This is a really important period of time," he explained. "We don't have any new components to test, but this is definitely a really important data point for us to understand and make some changes setup-wise, and try some things that we can potentially use to see if everything's working.

"There's some big changes for next year. But otherwise, right now we also have the focus on trying to make sure we maintain second in the Constructors' Championship. That's the focus."

Leclerc echoed his team mate's desire to finish the campaign positively, explaining that maintaining momentum heading into the winter break would be important for morale within Ferrari, while admitting that he is more concerned with securing further victories than his final Drivers' Championship position.

"My main focus at the moment is to try and win races, and the natural result of winning races will hopefully be second place in the Drivers' Championship," he said.

"I just want to finish the season on a high, for sure, in order to keep that good momentum. It's always important to finish the season on a high, particularly because the winter break is quite long, and for the motivation of everyone, it would be nice."

However, the Monegasque driver acknowledged that Ferrari could face another challenging weekend in Las Vegas, with cold temperatures and the circuit's long straights presenting particular concerns following the team's struggles with tyre warm-up in Brazil.

"We don't have any quick fixes, otherwise we would have put them on the car a long time ago," Leclerc admitted.

"There are things we cannot change now, and there are things that we can control and put our focus on. And that is the tyre warm-up, for example, that will be quite critical.

"If we do a very good job on that, I think it can outweigh maybe the disadvantage that we have power unit-wise. I remain hopeful, but it's going to be a big challenge for us."

title: ‘No excuse’: Ollie Bearman frustrated by lack of Haas F1 contract with 3 races left
Fenway Sports Group needs Brad Keselowski’s approval to buy into Cadillac F1
article_text:
Fenway Sports Group’s reported pursuit of an ownership stake in the Cadillac Formula 1 Team could be stalled by an unexpected roadblock: a NASCAR driver.

FSG, which also owns Liverpool and the Boston Red Sox, is among several parties in talks to buy billionaire Mark Walter’s stake in the Cadillac F1 team. But two racing industry sources familiar with the agreement told The Athletic that driver Brad Keselowski and FSG’s contract stipulates that neither can pursue a motorsports venture outside NASCAR without the other’s permission.

title: Charles Leclerc on journalist ban: “I was surprised by the choice of words”
article_text:
For Ferrari fans. The latest Scuderia Ferrari F1 news, driver updates, technical analysis and race reaction from Maranello and beyond.

Charles Leclerc had no hand in getting a veteran Formula 1 reporter barred from the paddock, and he isn't interested in policing the press - even when the headlines get a little personal.

Addressing the media ahead of the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, the Ferrari driver spoke for the first time about the FIA’s decision to revoke Daily Mail journalist Jonathan McEvoy’s accreditation for the remaining three rounds of the season.

"I saw the article; I was quite surprised by the choice of words, but apart from that I don’t have much to say," Leclerc said. "Then on the sanction itself, obviously I’ve got absolutely nothing to do with it, and I don’t have much to say about it."

Despite his surprise at the column, Leclerc drew a line between routine media scrutiny and the specific phrasing McEvoy used.

"The only thing I’ll say is that as Formula 1 drivers, I think we are used to this kind of criticism. Not this kind of criticism, but to criticism in general and to critics," Leclerc clarified. "It’s definitely the job of journalists to kind of ask the bad questions and do some of the tough headlines sometimes. But I was surprised with the choice of words."

The controversy began after McEvoy published an opinion piece reflecting on the opening-lap contact between Leclerc and Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton at the Mexico City Grand Prix, in which he referred to Leclerc as a "sneaky little b*****d".

FIA general manager Alberto Villarreal subsequently notified McEvoy that his accreditation was suspended for Las Vegas, Qatar, and Abu Dhabi, though he is expected to return for the 2027 season. Confirming the sanction, an FIA spokesperson cited the 2026 Formula 1 world championship guidelines, stating that media passes are issued at the governing body's sole discretion and require "the highest standards of fairness and professionalism".

title: Rafael Camara torn between his F2 title bid and more F1 races with Haas
article_text:
Rafael Camara is torn between completing his title-contending Formula 2 campaign and seeing out the 2026 season at Haas in Formula 1.

The Ferrari protege is the reigning F3 champion and leads the F2 standings as a rookie with Invicta Racing, courtesy of a starring campaign in which he has taken five pole positions and seven feature race podiums including three victories.

Esteban Ocon’s fallout with Haas has provided Camara with an opportunity to make his F1 debut at the Brazilian Grand Prix, and he will gain more experience this weekend in Las Vegas ahead of his full rookie campaign with the team in 2027.

However, the last two rounds of the F2 season are taking place alongside F1 in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, so Camara, Haas and Ferrari now have a tough call to make – with the youngster indicating “a mix of people” will be involved in the decision-making.

Asked about the situation, the 21-year-old replied: “Well, that's a very good question. Both of them will be very important for me. In F2, I feel like the whole year you're working for that and for sure you want to finish in a high. And also, I wouldn't be in this position or having the opportunities if it didn't happen, what happened this year in F2 with Invicta. So, for sure, it would be very special.

“At the end of the day, I'll be doing what I love to do, and I'll be happy in doing [either] of them. But it will definitely be a difficult decision to do on my side, because one side, you have Formula 1, something you've always been dreaming of being and doing in your life; and the other side, you have the whole championship and you're working the whole year to close that.

“Let's see. I'll try now to focus on this weekend and finish in a good way. And then hopefully we can sort it out, what will happen after that.”

Interestingly, FIA regulations mean no driver can compete in both F1 and F2 on the same weekend; if Camara does race in the feeder series, Haas can resort to reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa, who made an unexpected grand prix debut in Mexico after Ocon was suddenly dismissed.

Though he currently leads the F2 standings, the Invicta racer is just seven points ahead of Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov, who has missed out on a 2027 F1 graduation with Racing Bulls. Alpine academy members Alex Dunne and Gabriele Mini are respectively 18 and 44 points adrift.

Asked by Motorsport.com how valuable the F2 title would be to his CV and career, Camara commented: “Yeah, I think that would be nice, finishing the F2 season. And for sure, when you [look back on] what you achieved on the junior categories, I think it's something very nice, having the F3 and F2 championship, winning as a rookie. Not only that, but the feeling of winning and doing things will be very nice.

“But I still don't know what will happen and I don't know how I will do it. Like I said, I'm just trying to finish this weekend and then for sure there will be a lot of things to discuss after.”

Haas’ new driver is feeling much more confident ahead of his second grand prix, having gained key experience in tricky wet conditions on his way to a lowly 20th at Interlagos.

“The main takeaways were working with the team and also with how the car behaves,” Camara said of his maiden outing as a race driver. “I think it makes you already starting this weekend much calmer, because in a way you know what to expect.

“It helps starting the weekend with less things in your head, so you can, in a way, focus more into details, more in other things. Probably in Brazil, you're just trying to learn everything at the same time and your brain starts to overheat a bit. For sure it helps.”

title: Fernando Alonso rules out staying in F1 for V8 return: "16 years of pure racing lost"
article_text:
Although the FIA's formal confirmation on Tuesday was only online for a few minutes before being temporarily taken down again, it is clear to everyone in the paddock that V8 engines will return to Formula 1.

The agreement in principle involves a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 – with the turbo being particularly important for Audi and Honda – and a significantly smaller electrical component. The target for its introduction is 2030, which would be a year earlier than initially planned.

It is largely what the drivers have been pushing for, which explains the positive reactions in the Las Vegas paddock during the media day.

Fernando Alonso, however, stressed to media including Motorsport.com that the V8 return will come too late for him. The Spaniard is currently 45 and, perhaps unsurprisingly, has no intention of remaining in the pinnacle of motorsport for another four years: "No, I will not be around for the new V8. 100%."

When it was pointed out that Alonso has surprised people in the paddock before, for example with his F1 comeback in 2021, he laughed: "Yeah, I have surprised myself in the past as well! But this time I think it's the good one. When I stop, it will be the moment, also the moment to try different things.

"It's still a long way ahead, [the V8 return], but I think it will be enough [for me before that]."

Alonso does find it frustrating, in a sense, that he will have to bow out under a set of regulations that he, like many other drivers, is far from fond of: "Yes, it's frustrating that we didn't have it in 2014 already. From 2014 to 2030 or 2031, so that means 16 years or 17 years of pure racing are lost."

While Alonso will no longer be competing in F1 by then, he still has his sights set on other racing categories. Even after retiring from F1, Alonso intends to continue racing for a long time.

In January 2027, he will make an appearance at the Dakar Rally, but he is also leaving the door open to other iconic races once his F1 career comes to an end.

"Dakar was on my mind. Le Mans is on my mind, the Indy 500 is on my mind," the Aston Martin driver said.

"I love competing and I love competing in race cars in which you have power when you go on throttle, and in which you have deceleration when you brake. Those are the things that we miss now in Formula 1.

"Obviously, if I continue in Formula 1, that will always be my priority and it's difficult to put things together or to combine different programs. Dakar, because it's in January, it fits a little bit better, but even that had to come with a few coincidences."

That Alonso would like to return to endurance races such as Le Mans is no surprise – he would even like to do so alongside Max Verstappen – but his mention of the Indy 500 is somewhat more unexpected.

After his last attempt in 2020, the Spaniard did not seem particularly keen on another appearance at The Greatest Spectacle in Racing at the Brickyard, but with a new IndyCar chassis on the way, his opinion could change.

"Yeah, I don't know. They will change cars soon. There's a new car coming for 2028, I think, so yeah, I don't know," he said. "I may consider it one day. It’s not in my short-term plans and not on my mind now, but I cannot say no to it 100%."

title: Bank of America Youth Sports Platform Sports with Us Launches in Italy With PlayMore!
article_text:
- Bank of America named PlayMore! as the delivery partner for its Sports with Us youth sports platform in Italy, announced November 16 in Milan.

- Sports with Us now spans 15 countries and provides access to sports for more than 1.2 million children, according to the bank.

- The Italy launch expands the PlayMore! United program, pairing weekly training sessions with lessons in leadership, nutrition and financial education.

- Outside the U.S., the bank aims to positively impact more than 10,000 young people across 14 countries by the end of 2028.

Bank of America has named PlayMore!, an established sport-for-development organization, as the delivery partner for Sports with Us in Italy. The launch extends the Bank of America youth sports platform, which the bank says now spans 15 countries and provides access to sports for more than 1.2 million children, according to its November 16, 2026 announcement from Milan.

Sports with Us combines sport, mentoring and education with the stated goal of helping young people build confidence, develop life skills and access pathways to education, per the release.

The Italian rollout will support the expansion of the PlayMore! United program, which pairs regular sport participation with structured life-skills development. Participants will attend weekly “United” training sessions alongside practical learning in leadership, teamwork, communication, wellbeing, nutrition and financial education, the bank said.

According to the release, the curriculum modules were built specifically for Sports with Us in collaboration with global universities and educational institutions, which were not named. The bank’s FAQ adds that sport-based activities are led by Athlete Mentors.

Vito Luca Lo Piccolo, Country Executive for Bank of America Italy, framed the program around access: “Sport has the power to open doors.” He said the partnership with PlayMore! is meant to create pathways for young people to build brighter futures.

Who Is PlayMore!, the Italy Delivery Partner?

PlayMore! has worked on an inclusion principle since 2010, according to President Luigi De Micco, who said the organization believes “sport brings people together on equal terms, regardless of their starting point.” De Micco said Sports with Us lets PlayMore! extend that approach to more young people in Milan and across Italy, with added focus on confidence, wellbeing and independence.

Najla Aqdeir, a coach and ambassador for PlayMore!, said she sees daily how teamwork, discipline, leadership and resilience learned through sport carry into other parts of young people’s lives.

Bank of America describes Sports with Us as part of its commitment to leave a lasting legacy after serving as the Official Bank of the FIFA World Cup 2026. Outside the United States, the bank says the platform supports an ambition to positively impact more than 10,000 young people across 14 countries by the end of 2028.

Italy follows the United Kingdom, where Bank of America named the Youth Sport Trust as its Sports with Us delivery partner, building on an existing relationship. The Youth Sport Trust, founded in 1995, works with around 20,000 schools and provides opportunities for more than two million children each year, according to the organization.

The structure in both markets is the same: the bank’s platform is delivered by an established local organization with its own existing programming. In Italy, that means weekly United sessions in Milan with a stated path to other parts of the country.

The release does not disclose the size of Bank of America’s financial commitment, how many participants PlayMore! United will reach, or which Italian cities follow Milan, the figures that will show how much of the 10,000-person target Italy is expected to carry.

Youth Sports Business Report (YSBR) is the largest and most trusted media platform covering the business of youth sports worldwide. YSBR delivers youth sports news, market intelligence, and original analysis daily across facilities, sponsorships, private equity, NIL, sports technology, and league operations. With more than 50,000 followers, YSBR is the leading source of youth sports industry news for the investors, owners, operators, and brands shaping the future of youth sports.

American families spend approximately $54 billion annually on kids’ sports and recreation, according to the YSBR and Kinetica Group Youth Sports TAM & Parent Spending Report, with organized sports alone representing a $40 billion-plus market. The average family spent $1,016 on a child’s primary sport in 2024, up 46 percent since 2019, per the Aspen Institute’s Project Play, and market research projects the global youth sports market will reach approximately $114 billion by 2032 (Business Research Insights).

How many kids play youth sports in the United States?

Approximately 27.3 million children ages 6 to 17, or about 54.6 percent, played organized sports in 2022-2023, according to the National Survey of Children’s Health as reported by the Aspen Institute’s Project Play. High school sports participation reached a record 8.26 million athletes in 2024-25, per the NFHS.

Youth Sports Business Report was founded by Cameron Korab, a sports marketing veteran with more than a decade in the industry and an MBA from Northwestern University’s Kellogg School of Management.
